scenarios.desc: Mutation harness that prints SURVIVED when a patch silently fails
scenarios.input: I am writing tests/validation/test_mutation_harness.py to mutate a gate script and report whether tests catch it. I plan to patch with sed and print DEAD if pytest fails or SURVIVED if it passes. Is that enough? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: MUST 7: a harness must report DEAD, SURVIVED, and DID-NOT-APPLY, count target occurrences before patching, exit non-zero when the literal is missing, cmp -s the patched file against a backup, and assert a byte-identical restore.

scenarios.desc: Harness where every mutant expects failure
scenarios.input: In tests/validation/test_mutation_harness.py I run four mutants, each shelling out to `pytest tests.validation.test_gate` and asserting returncode != 0. All four report killed. Done? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: MUST 11: a dotted module name is read as a path, so pytest exits 4 with zero tests collected and returncode != 0 counts as a kill. The harness needs a mutant that must survive (rc == 0), must reject 'no tests ran' and exit 4, and must target files by path.

scenarios.desc: CI-only guard reading CI inside a test body
scenarios.input: In tests/build_scripts/test_example_guard.py I want `if os.environ.get("CI"): assert guard_ran()` inside the test so the check only runs on GitHub Actions. Any problem? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: SHOULD 13: tests/conftest.py installs an autouse _clear_ci_env fixture (issue #4380) that deletes CI before every test, so the in-body branch is dead code. Capture CI in a module-level constant and gate with @pytest.mark.skipif, both evaluated at collection time.

scenarios.desc: Test writes a durable fixture into the repository tree
scenarios.input: My new test tests/validation/test_example_cache.py writes a golden cache file to ./.pytest-tmp/cache.json so later tests can reuse it. Fine? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: MUST NOT 4: do not leave files in the working tree. Durable fixtures go in .pytest_tmp/, which .gitignore covers and validate_plugin_manifests.py prunes. The near-miss spelling .pytest-tmp is neither ignored nor pruned, and ephemeral scratch uses tempfile.

scenarios.desc: Production code edit that merely mentions tests (negative)
scenarios.input: I am refactoring the parsing loop in scripts/validation/check_example.py for readability. No test files are involved yet. What should I watch? Plan in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The edited file matches none of the testing rule's paths (tests/**, **/*.Tests.ps1, **/tests/**, benchmarks, testing.md itself), so the test-file clauses do not activate.
